title: Starting a shared reading plan while signed out fails silently
summary: Before this change, someone who was signed out could open a shared reading plan link, choose a pace, click **Start plan**, and nothing would happen. Now **Start plan** asks them to sign in first and then starts the plan, and if starting fails for any other reason a message appears instead of nothing. Note: the issue also asks for a message when **Restart** on a plan fails; this PR doesn't change that, so T7 is expected to fail.

links.label: Issue 2086: Starting a shared reading plan while signed out fails silently

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a computer. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be finishing: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac.

setup.title: Sign in and make a reading plan to share
setup.body: Sign in with an email address you can check (the app emails you a code to type in). Open **Reading plans** and click **Create reading plan**. Name it `Shared start test` and continue to **Select readings**. In **Session 1**, add a **Scripture** reading `John 3`. Click **Add session**, and in **Session 2** add a **Scripture** reading `Psalm 23`. Finish with **Create plan**. If you can't find **Reading plans** anywhere in the app, reading plans aren't turned on for your account: mark every test **Blocked** and say so in a note.

setup.title: Copy the plan's share link
setup.body: In the **Reading plans** list, select the **⋮** button next to `Shared start test`, then **Share**, and copy the link. Paste it somewhere you can get to it again (a note or text file). Every test in the first two sections opens this link.

setup.title: Use a private window for the signed-out tests
setup.body: A private (incognito) window starts signed out: Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome or Edge, Ctrl+Shift+P in Firefox (Cmd instead of Ctrl on Mac). Open a **new** private window for each signed-out test so you always start fresh. Change the start of the copied link to the preview address if it points at seedbible.org: keep everything from `/en/reading-plan/` onwards and put `https://alpha.seedbible.org/b/fix__2086/93778f33bc7164b0e6fef5278d0747d57636a757` in front of it.

sections.title: Starting a shared plan while signed out
sections.intro: These tests are the bug from the issue. Do each one in a new private window.

tests.title: Clicking Start plan while signed out asks you to sign in
tests.why: This is the bug: before the fix, nothing happened at all.
steps: In a new private window, open the plan's share link (on the preview address).
Click **Start Reading Plan**.
In the side panel, leave the pace on its first choice (not **At my own pace**).
Click **Start plan**.
expected: The sign-in window opens, asking for your email.
No error message appears behind it.

tests.title: After signing in, the plan starts on its own
tests.why: The issue suggests the plan should start automatically once you sign in, so you don't have to click Start plan a second time.
tests.before: Continue straight on from T1, with the sign-in window still open.
steps: Sign in: type your email, then the code you're emailed.
Wait a few seconds after the sign-in window closes, without clicking anything else.
expected: The plan starts by itself: the side panel changes from the pace choice to the started plan, showing its first day or session.
You did not have to click **Start plan** again.

tests.title: Closing the sign-in window doesn't start the plan, and you can try again
tests.why: The issue doesn't say what should happen if you back out of signing in. The code at this commit may show the message "Couldn't start the reading plan. Please try again." here; note in your result whether it does, and whether that seems right to you.
steps: In a new private window, open the plan's share link, click **Start Reading Plan**, and click **Start plan**.
When the sign-in window opens, close it without signing in (its close button, or press Esc).
Look at the side panel, then click **Start plan** again.
expected: The plan does not start: the side panel still shows the pace choice and **Start plan**.
Clicking **Start plan** again opens the sign-in window again (it isn't stuck or greyed out).

tests.title: The same works with the At my own pace choice
steps: In a new private window, open the plan's share link and click **Start Reading Plan**.
In the side panel, choose **At my own pace**.
Click **Start plan**, and sign in when asked.
expected: After signing in, the plan starts at your own pace (no daily schedule shown) without clicking **Start plan** again.

sections.title: When starting fails for another reason
sections.intro: Use your normal (not private) window, signed in.

tests.title: A message appears when Start plan fails because you're offline
tests.why: The issue asks that a failure to start is never silent. Turning off your internet is the simplest way to make it fail.
tests.before: Signing in during T2 and T4 started `Shared start test` on your account, so make a fresh plan: create a second plan named `Offline test` the same way as in setup, and don't start it.
steps: Open **Reading plans**, open `Offline test`, and choose a pace.
Turn off Wi-Fi (or unplug the network cable, or turn on airplane mode).
Click **Start plan** and wait up to a minute.
Turn Wi-Fi back on.
expected: A message appears: **Couldn't start the reading plan. Please try again.**
**Start plan** can be clicked again afterwards.

tests.title: Signed in, Start plan starts the plan straight away
tests.why: Checks the new sign-in check doesn't get in the way when you're already signed in.
tests.before: Wi-Fi is back on. Create one more plan the same way as in setup, named `Signed in test`, and don't start it.
steps: Open **Reading plans**, open `Signed in test`, choose a pace, and click **Start plan**.
expected: The plan starts right away, with no sign-in window and no error message.

tests.title: A message appears when Restart fails because you're offline
tests.why: Issue 2086 asks for a message whenever starting a plan fails, and names the **Restart** button too; the code at this commit still fails silently there, so this test is expected to fail.
tests.before: You have at least one started plan in your **Reading plans** list.
steps: Open **Reading plans** and find a started plan with a **Restart** button.
Turn off Wi-Fi.
Click **Restart** and wait up to a minute.
Turn Wi-Fi back on.
expected: A message appears saying the plan couldn't be restarted.

notCovered: Other languages: the new message was only added in English, so other languages show the English text until translators add it.
